accepted.question_text: Let X be an affine scheme, let a be a finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field, and let an algebraic group Gamma act completely reducibly on both X and a. Classify the irreducible finite-dimensional representations of the equivariant map algebra M(X, a)^Gamma in this more general setting, where Gamma is no longer required to be finite.

evidence.quote: Instead of a finite group Γ, one can consider, for instance, an algebraic group acting completely reducibly on A and a.
The first step in the study of the resulting EMAs would be to classify their irreducible finite-dimensional representations.

accepted.question_text: For equivariant map algebras whose target algebra is not the finite-dimensional Lie or associative algebra considered in the standard theory, develop the representation theory of the resulting EMA. In particular, determine finite-dimensional representations when the target is a Kac-Moody algebra, the Heisenberg algebra, an alternative algebra, a Jordan algebra, or another algebra with a well-defined notion of representation.

evidence.quote: There are many possible choices for the 'target' algebra g for which the resulting EMA has not been studied.
For example, it would be natural to consider the finite-dimensional representations in the case of alternative algebras or Jordan algebras.

accepted.question_text: Extend the theory of equivariant map superalgebras by allowing more general target Lie superalgebras, replacing the coordinate algebra A by a supercommutative algebra so that X becomes a superscheme, and replacing Gamma by a Z2-graded group. Determine the resulting representation theory in this broader super setting.

evidence.quote: The equivariant map superalgebra setting of [Sav] can be naturally generalized.
Furthermore, one can replace A by a supercommutative algebra (in other words, let X be a superscheme) and Γ by a Z2-graded group.

accepted.question_text: Replace the algebraic setup of equivariant map algebras by an analytic one in which X is a Banach manifold, a is a Banach algebra, and one studies equivariant differentiable maps X to a. Build and analyze the corresponding analytic theory of equivariant map algebras and their representations.

evidence.quote: Another interesting problem is to replace the algebraic setting by an analytic one.
For example, let X be a Banach manifold, a a Banach algebra and consider equivariant differentiable maps X → a.

accepted.question_text: Characterize equivariant map algebras up to isomorphism in substantially greater generality. In particular, generalize known isomorphism results for loop and multiloop algebras to broader multiloop situations and then to more general equivariant map algebras M(X, a)^Gamma.

evidence.quote: Characterizing EMAs up to isomorphism is one of the fundamental problems in the theory of EMAs.
It is therefore natural, though likely difficult, to try to generalize the results of both papers [ABP] and [GP07] to the multiloop case and beyond that to more general EMAs.

accepted.question_text: Determine the automorphism groups of equivariant map algebras M(X, a)^Gamma in broad generality, including twisted and multiloop cases, as part of understanding how these algebras are characterized and related to one another.

evidence.quote: Related to the problem of characterizing EMAs up to isomorphism, is the question of determining the automorphism groups of EMAs.

accepted.question_text: Let M = M(X, a)^Gamma with a a finite-dimensional associative algebra. Go beyond the classification of irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules and describe all indecomposable finite-dimensional modules, together with the block decomposition of the finite-dimensional module category.

evidence.quote: Ideally, one would like to describe all of the indecomposable finite-dimensional modules and understand the block decomposition of this category.

accepted.question_text: When the target algebra a is an associative bialgebra, use the comultiplication on a to define and analyze multi-orbit evaluation representations of the equivariant map algebra M(X, a)^Gamma, and determine their structure and role in the representation theory.

evidence.quote: In the case that a is an associative bialgebra, one can naturally define multi-orbit evaluation representations using the comultiplication on a.
It would be interesting to understand these representations.

accepted.question_text: For an equivariant map Lie algebra M = M(X, g)^Gamma, compute higher extension groups between finite-dimensional modules, not just Ext^1, and explain how those higher Ext groups and the global dimension of the finite-dimensional module category depend on the geometry of the scheme X.

evidence.quote: Only the first Ext groups are calculated in [NS].

It is natural to try to compute higher Ext groups. One would expect a rich interplay between these groups and the geometry of the scheme X. It would be particularly interesting to see how the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional modules is related to this geometry.

accepted.question_text: Extend the theory of global and local Weyl modules from current and loop algebras to more arbitrary equivariant map Lie algebras. In particular, determine lengths, dimensions, and characters of local Weyl modules in that general setting, and decide whether a suitable form of BGG reciprocity also holds for general EMAs.

evidence.quote: In particular, one would like to extend the results on the lengths, dimensions and characters of the local Weyl modules (see [CP01, BN04, CL06, CM04, FL07, Nak01, Nao12]) to the setting of more arbitrary EMAs (see [FMSa] for the definitions of global and local Weyl modules in this setting).
It is also natural to try to extend the notion of BGG reciprocity described in [BCM12, BBC+] to a more general EMA setting.

accepted.question_text: Develop the theory of possibly infinite-dimensional representations of equivariant map Lie algebras beyond the finite-dimensional case. In particular, define and study analogues of category O, the category of integrable highest weight representations, the category of quasifinite representations with finite-dimensional weight spaces, and related representation-theoretic frameworks for general EMAs.

evidence.quote: Much of the current focus in the study of the representation theory of arbitrary EMAs has been on the category of finite-dimensional representations.

It would be interesting to study analogous categories in the more arbitrary EMA setting. For example, one could consider the category of integrable highest weight representations, the category of quasifinite representations (i.e. representations with finite-dimensional weight spaces) or appropriate generalizations of category O.

accepted.question_text: For a semisimple-target equivariant map Lie algebra M and a general M-module V, describe the cohomology and homology of M in greater generality: determine H^1(M, V), understand the special case H^1(M, M_ad) related to derivations, and determine the groups H_*(M, V), including how perfectness and representation-theoretic structure are reflected in these invariants.

evidence.quote: One can therefore expect that it should be possible to describe the first cohomology group H1(M, V ) for a general M-module V .
A related problem is to determine the homology groups H∗(M, V ).

accepted.question_text: For a perfect equivariant map Lie algebra (g tensor A)^Gamma, determine its central extensions, preferably the universal central extension, and decide in broad generality whether the natural comparison formula uce((g tensor A)^Gamma) is isomorphic to the Gamma-fixed subalgebra of uce(g tensor A).

evidence.quote: It is therefore of interest to understand central extensions of equivariant map algebras M, preferably the universal central extension uce(M) of a perfect M.
The formula one is aiming for is then very natural: uce((g⊗A)^Γ) ≅ (uce(g⊗A))^Γ.

trace.notes: Mapped the paper as a survey on equivariant map algebras with sections on general EMAs, associative EMAs, Lie EMAs, and a dedicated open problems section. The open-problem material is concentrated in Section 4 on pages 13-16.
Extracted research directions from Section 4.1 on new types of equivariant map algebras, covering more general groups, targets, super settings, and analytic settings.
Extracted general EMA open problems from Section 4.2, including isomorphisms, automorphisms, indecomposable modules, and associative bialgebra evaluation representations.
Extracted Lie-theoretic open problems from Section 4.3, including higher extensions, Weyl modules, broader representation categories, cohomology, homology, and central extensions.
Rewrote 13 extracted items into standalone questions by inlining the EMA setting M(X, a)^Gamma or M(X, g)^Gamma and preserving only claims directly supported by the quoted text.

Kept 13 distinct questions. Closely related themes such as cohomology versus central extensions and new targets versus super/analytic generalizations were treated as separate non-duplicate problems because the paper states them separately.
All accepted items have page-numbered verbatim evidence, use self-contained wording, and avoid unresolved references to sections or propositions.
